I'm trying to figure out the connection rule — it seems like the path links blocks that are aligned by row or column with each other, like a maze connecting them from the starting block, though I need to check which pairs actually get connected versus not.

Checking train3, I trace a similar path starting from the "2" block and snaking through aligned neighbors, alternating horizontal and vertical connections, until it reaches the last block — leaving at least one block like (4,5) unconnected, suggesting the path doesn't touch every block, only a specific chain.

For train1, I see the 2 only connects in one direction to the nearest aligned block, since the other side has a bigger gap, and the chain stops there with no further connections. For train4, I confirm the 2 connects upward to the nearest aligned block in its column, continuing the same nearest-neighbor logic.

Trying train3, I follow the chain but hit an inconsistency—it seems like the path doesn't strictly alternate horizontal/vertical, so maybe the actual rule is simply always jumping to the nearest unvisited aligned block regardless of direction, and I'm testing that against the observed path.

Then applying this greedy-nearest hypothesis to train4, tracing through each block's row/column distances to see if it matches the pattern.

Now I'm verifying train2 by tracing the sequence of block connections through their shared rows and columns, checking each link against the output pairs like (21,2)-(21,7), (11,7)-(11,3), and (6,3)-(6,14).

Continuing the chain: (11,3) to (6,3), then (6,3) jumps to (6,14) since nothing connects upward, then (6,14) to (11,14), then down to (21,14), then across to (21,21) closing out that path. The remaining points like (1,1) and (15,24) look fine on their own, so I'll move on to testing this layout.

I'm mapping out block positions on the grid and tracing possible paths between them, checking gaps along shared rows and columns to find the shortest connecting route from (3,4) through (3,11) toward (8,11).

Continuing the traversal, I find each next block by checking row/column alignment and picking the smallest gap: (8,11)→(8,7)→(14,7)→(14,4)→(19,4)→(19,13), then confirm no further moves remain. Each connecting segment spans a consistent length of 7 across rows or columns, so I'm laying out all seven draw segments accordingly.
